vision: Credible, dynamic, and independent central bank, with a high calibre team, committed to improving the well-being of the people of Pakistan.
mission: Maintain price and financial stability, with a technologically advanced financial system, for inclusive and sustainable economic development of Pakistan.
values: Stand behind commitments, act impartially, protect confidential information.
Own decisions and outcomes; welcome independent review and feedback.
Challenge the status quo; use technology to serve stakeholders.
Value diverse skills; gender mainstreaming; equal-opportunity employer.
Fairness, compassion, work-life balance, health and safety.
Save energy, cut carbon, move to a paperless office.
goals: Maintain inflation within the medium-term target range
Enhance efficiency, effectiveness, fairness and stability of the financial system
Promote inclusive and sustainable access to financial services
Transform to a Shariah-compliant banking system
Build an innovative and inclusive digital financial services ecosystem
Transform SBP into a high-tech, people-centric organization
stakeholders: Appoints top officials; fiscal policy affects inflation
Programme conditions on rates, laws and independence
Passes and amends the SBP Act
Regulated by SBP; directly hit by every decision

cases.title: Autonomy law
cases.power: Legitimate power shifts from government to SBP
cases.text: The SBP (Amendment) Act, passed in January 2022 during IMF talks, made price stability SBP's main goal, ended government borrowing from SBP and removed the Finance Secretary's vote on the Board. Critics called it a loss of economic sovereignty.

cases.title: Interest-free banking ruling
cases.text: The Federal Shariat Court (April 2022) ordered a fully Shariah-compliant banking system by December 2027. SBP appealed, then withdrew the appeal in November 2022 after the government's decision.

cases.title: Emergency hike to 22%
cases.text: An unscheduled MPC meeting on 26 June 2023 raised the policy rate to a record 22%, citing new budget taxes; analysts linked it to completing the IMF programme.

cases.title: IMF on SBP's board
cases.text: An IMF governance report asked Pakistan to remove the Finance Secretary from SBP's board entirely and to fill vacant deputy-governor posts quickly.

cases.title: Dual-nationality dispute
cases.text: The 2022 law barred dual nationals from top SBP posts. A deputy-governor post stayed vacant about 21 months; the cabinet refused to relax the rule and Muhammad Ali Malik was appointed in August 2026.

cases.title: Executive pay up 94%
cases.text: SBP's FY2025-26 financial statements showed the combined pay and benefits of the Governor and Deputy Governors rising from Rs94m to Rs183m, attracting media criticism.

Strengths: Strong legal authority and clear mandate
Weaknesses: Technical language is hard for the public
Opportunities: More women in finance (Banking on Equality)
Threats: Political and IMF pressure on independence
